# T03 — implement `crates/rivet-core/src/object/tag.rs` (19 bodies)

## Scope

**ONE file only: `crates/rivet-core/src/object/tag.rs`.** Do not edit any other file. No new
dependencies. Doc comments, signatures, types, lifetimes and public items are FROZEN: do not
change, rename, add or remove any of them.

Goal: replace all **19** `todo!()` bodies, add a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of
tag.rs, and finish with `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` clean and
`cargo test -p rivet-core` green (the 41 tests that exist today must keep passing, plus yours).

## The 19 items

`impl Tag`: `kind()` · `parse()` · `to_bytes()` · `write_to()` · `id()` · `object()` · `name()` ·
`tagger()` · `message()` · `signature()` · `is_signed()` — 11 bodies.

`impl TagBuilder`: `new()` · `object()` · `kind()` · `name()` · `tagger()` · `message()` ·
`signature()` · `build()` — 8 bodies.

15 of these are one-liners (accessors return the public field; the setters assign and return
`self`). Only `parse` and `build` are substantive. `parse` is ~90% of the work.

## APIs that exist — use exactly these, invent nothing

- `Signature::parse(data: &BStr) -> Result<Signature>` (commit.rs:101).
- `Signature::to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>` (commit.rs:161).
- `ObjectId::from_hex(format: ObjectFormat, hex: <byte slice>) -> Result<ObjectId>` (hash.rs:247)
  — for the `object` header, whose value is hex **text**. `from_bytes` takes *raw bytes* and is
  the wrong call here (it compiles and silently hashes garbage).
- `ObjectId::to_hex(&self)`.
- `hash_object(format, kind, data: &[u8]) -> Result<(ObjectId, Vec<u8>)>` (object/mod.rs:137)
  — returns `(id, full_buffer)`; take `.0`.
- `ObjectKind::as_bytes()` — the exact lowercase wire word (`blob`/`tree`/`commit`/`tag`).
- `bstr::BStr::new(&[u8]) -> &BStr` (both `BStr`/`BString` are already imported).
- Error variants (error.rs): `MalformedObject { kind, reason: String }` @245,
  `MissingHeader { kind, header: &'static str }` @247,
  `InvalidHeader { kind, header: &'static str, reason: &'static str }` @259, `Message(String)`,
  and the `std::io::Error` variant for `write_to` (read error.rs to see its shape).
- `parse_decimal` / `parse_tz_offset` in commit.rs are **private** and not reachable — you do not
  need them; `Signature::parse` handles the tagger line whole.

## `parse` — exact algorithm

1. **Boundary.** Find the first `"\n\n"` (the blank line after the headers). If there is none,
   return `MalformedObject { kind: Tag, reason: "no blank line after headers" }`.
   Message region = everything after those two bytes.
2. **Header lines.** Walk the header region line by line (split on `\n`). For each non-empty line,
   split at the **first space**: name before, value after. A line with **no space** is
   `MalformedObject { reason: "header line has no space after its name" }`. Strip nothing else —
   the value is the bytes up to the line end, with no trailing `\n` (the value itself is not
   trimmed).
3. **Known headers**, keyed by name (not by position):
   - `object` → `ObjectId::from_hex(format, value)`; on error
     `InvalidHeader { header: "object", reason: "not a valid object id for this format" }`.
   - `type` → `blob`/`tree`/`commit`/`tag` → `ObjectKind`; anything else
     `InvalidHeader { header: "type", reason: "unknown object kind" }`.
   - `tag` → the name, stored as `&'a BStr` borrowed from `data` (never trimmed, may be empty).
   - `tagger` → `Signature::parse(value.as_bstr())`; on `Err`
     `InvalidHeader { header: "tagger", reason: "malformed signature" }` (do not forward the inner
     error; the field is `&'static str`).
   - **Any other name → skip it silently.** Unknown headers are not modelled; they survive through
     `raw` only. Do not error on them.
   - Duplicate names: **first occurrence wins**, later duplicates are ignored.
4. **Required headers.** `object`, `type`, `tag`, `tagger` — a missing one is
   `MissingHeader { kind: Tag, header: "<name>" }`. (See D1 for `tagger`.)
5. **Signature scan.** In the message region only, find an **armour line starting a line**: index 0
   of the region, or immediately after a `\n`. Four headers count:
   `-----BEGIN PGP SIGNATURE-----`, `-----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----`,
   `-----BEGIN SIGNED MESSAGE-----`, `-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----`. Testing PGP alone is the
   failure the module docs warn about.
6. **Split.** `message = data[msg_start .. sig_start]` — the newline that precedes the armour
   line **stays in the message**. `signature = data[sig_start ..]` — through the end of the body,
   armour and trailing newline included. No armour found → `message` is the whole message region
   and `signature` is `None`.
7. Store `raw = data`; `message`, `name`, `signature` all borrow from `data`.

`message` may be empty (legal), may contain blank lines, and is never trimmed. Return
`Result<Self>` — never index or slice without bounds checks.

## `to_bytes` / `write_to` / `id`

- `to_bytes`: if `!self.raw.is_empty()` return `self.raw.to_vec()` (a parsed tag round-trips
  byte-for-byte — this is the property the differential tests check). Otherwise rebuild:
  `object <hex>\ntype <kind>\ntag <name>\ntagger <sig bytes>\n\n<message>` then the signature
  **appended with no separator** (a blank line before it breaks verification).
- `write_to`: the same bytes as `to_bytes`, `Error` from the io failure.
- `id`: mirror `Commit::id` (commit.rs:484) with `ObjectKind::Tag`.

## Ambiguities I have already decided — implement these, do not re-open them

- **D1 — missing `tagger` line:** `MissingHeader { kind: Tag, header: "tagger" }`. Real git
  tolerates a tagger-less tag (it only warns), but `Tag::tagger` is not an `Option`, so Rivet
  cannot represent it and must fail loudly. No doc-comment change is permitted; just implement it.
- **D2 — `TagBuilder::build` with `kind: None`:** `MissingHeader { kind: Tag, header: "type" }`.
  `build` takes no object database, so it cannot resolve the kind; the caller sets it.
- **D3 — `build` with `object: None`:** `MissingHeader { header: "object" }`. With no `tagger`:
  `Error::Message("cannot resolve tagger identity: set GIT_COMMITTER_NAME or user.name")` —
  exactly the shape of `CommitBuilder::build` (commit.rs:679-694).
- **D4** — the tag name is **not** validated in `build` (no ref-format check; that is the CLI's job).
- **D5** — duplicate headers: first wins (see 3 above).

## Tests you must add (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the end of tag.rs)

Each must fail if the logic is wrong; build the fixtures as byte literals, no external `git` call.
Use the module-doc example body as one fixture (it is a real, valid body).

1. round-trip: a four-header body with a trailing-newline message → `to_bytes() == input` and
   `id(format) == hash_object(format, Tag, input)?.0`.
2. `object`/`type`/`tag`/`tagger` parse to the expected values.
3. signed tag: message `"the tag message\n"` + PGP armour → `message() == b"the tag message\n"`
   (the newline before the armour is the message's) and `is_signed()`, `signature()` correct.
4. `-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----` is recognised too (and `SIGNED MESSAGE`, `PGP MESSAGE`).
5. a message containing a blank line: the blank line does not end the message and does not split
   the signature.
6. an unsigned tag with an empty message: `message()` empty, `signature()` `None`, `is_signed()`
   false — legal, not an error.
7. missing `tagger` → `MissingHeader { header: "tagger" }` (D1).
8. unknown header (`extra foo`) is skipped and the round trip is still exact.
9. header line with no space → `MalformedObject`.
10. `type quux` → `InvalidHeader`; 11. `object <bad hex>` → `InvalidHeader`.
12. no blank line after the headers → `MalformedObject`.
13. `Tag::kind() == ObjectKind::Tag` (not the target's kind).
14. `TagBuilder`: `new()` is empty; `build` without `object` → `MissingHeader`; without `tagger` →
    `Message` (D3); without `kind` → `MissingHeader` (D2); a fully-set builder writes
    `type commit` and `parse(build())` gives back the same object/name/message.
15. `signature()` appended by the builder: `parse` of the built bytes finds it (the builder writes
    the armour, so it must be found at a line start).
